issues.description: Method name mismatch for the total-students accessor: problem_statement.md (line 41) refers to get_total_number_of_students() using snake_case, while the UML, the template TODO comment, and the solution implementation use the camelCase name getTotalNumberOfStudents(). This inconsistency can confuse students about the exact method identifier to implement and may cause them to implement a name that does not match the tests or the provided UML.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Update problem_statement.md to use the camelCase name getTotalNumberOfStudents() to match the UML, template, and solution. If snake_case was intentional, instead update the UML, template TODO, and solution implementation to use get_total_number_of_students() and adapt tests accordingly. Prefer camelCase to follow Java naming conventions.

issues.description: Method name for the same concept (total number of students) is inconsistent across artifacts: the problem statement text refers to get_total_number_of_students() (snake_case) while the UML diagram and both code artifacts (template TODO and solution implementation) use the Java-style camelCase getTotalNumberOfStudents(). A student reading the instructions could be unsure whether to implement get_total_number_of_students() (exactly as written in the prose) or getTotalNumberOfStudents() (as shown in the UML and template/solution), which may lead to compilation failures or test mismatches.
issues.suggestedFix: Edit problem_statement.md to use the camelCase method name getTotalNumberOfStudents() (replace get_total_number_of_students() at line 41). Also add a brief note that the implementation should use the Java-style camelCase method name to match the UML and the template/solution, ensuring consistent naming across all artifacts.
